rca of the issue: Slug normalisation bug — routers/public.py line 132 reads `desired_slug = (body.slug or '').lower().strip() or c.get('transparency_slug') or _make_slug(c['name'])`. The trailing `_make_slug(c['name'])` branch is only hit when body.slug is empty AND the company has no existing slug. For ANY non-empty body.slug, only .lower() and .strip() are applied, allowing characters like '!', '@', spaces (after strip, internal spaces survive), '$', etc. to be persisted. Reproduction: POST /api/public/transparency/admin/toggle with {enabled:true, slug:' Demo-Salone-TEST!!@@ '} → DB stores 'demo-salone-test!!@@'. Mitigation: change the line to `desired_slug = _make_slug(body.slug) if (body.slug and body.slug.strip()) else (c.get('transparency_slug') or _make_slug(c['name']))`. Bonus: also reject empty post-normalisation result with 400.
